dedupe_keys.name: ejatlas global atlas of environmental justice

description: A global map and database of social conflicts over environmental issues, including mining, dams, oil and gas, industry and waste. The EJAtlas home page says 4,586 cases have been reported so far, that it is a work in progress with cases continuously added, and that the absence of data does not mean the absence of conflict. The Western Mining Action Network page that embeds its mining map says the atlas is directed at ICTA-UAB by Leah Temper and Joan Martinez Alier, coordinated by Daniela Del Bene, and was supported by the ENVJUST ERC grant and the ACKnowl-EJ project; the EJOLT project page hosts the earlier maps. The atlas is free to browse and filter online. Coverage is worldwide, one entry per conflict. Caveats: entries are written by activists and researchers, so coverage is uneven, and the licence and a bulk download are not stated on the pages read. For simulation it shows where mines, dams and industrial sites face community opposition, which can delay projects or disrupt supply. A related catalogue record is the WRI mining concessions dataset.
